title: Straight-Line Reflection Mapping via Geometry
approach_explanation:
When a ball travels on a square table of side length $s$ at $45^	ext{circ}$ angles, its trajectory can be modeled by reflecting the table across its boundaries infinitely. In this unfolded plane, a trajectory is just a straight ray. Since pockets are located at $(0,0)$, $(0,s)$, $(s,0)$, and $(s,s)$, a ball will eventually reach a pocket if and only if its initial position $(x_i, y_i)$ and velocity direction $(dx, dy)$ lie directly on one of the diagonals of the square table that lead straight to a corner. Specifically, for a trajectory moving with slope $+1$, the condition is $x_i = y_i$ when $dx = dy$, or $y_i = s - x_i$ when $dx 
eq dy$. This reduces the problem of simulating ball bounces to simple coordinate checks per ball.

code_breakdown.explanation: Reads the number of test cases $t$, and for each test case reads $n$ (the number of balls) and $s$ (the side length of the table).
Iterates through all $n$ balls, reading their direction vectors $dx, dy$ and initial positions $xi, yi$.

Checks if the ball is already on a trajectory aligned directly with a pocket. A ball with $dx = dy$ will hit a pocket if $xi = yi$. A ball with $dx 
eq dy$ will hit a pocket if $yi = s - xi$. If either condition holds, the pocket counter is incremented.
Prints the total number of potted balls for each testcase.

complexity_analysis.time_justification: For each of the $t$ test cases, we loop $n$ times where $n$ is the number of balls. Inside the loop, we perform a constant number of $O(1)$ arithmetic and logical comparisons. Thus, the total time complexity is $O(	ext{sum of } n)$, which is bounded by $10^3$ operations across all test cases.
complexity_analysis.space_justification: Only a few scalar variables ($t, n, s, dx, dy, xi, yi, pockets$) are used to process the inputs on-the-fly, requiring constant auxiliary memory beyond standard I/O buffers.

strengths: Avoids complex and slow physical simulations by leveraging mathematical insight.
Optimal $O(N)$ time complexity and $O(1)$ space complexity.
edge_cases_handled: Handles both diagonal types ($y = x$ and $y = s - x$).
Supports all four quadrant velocity combinations ($dx, dy ∈ \{-1, 1\}$).
